title: Dip buyer
oneLiner: An agent that waits for coins you picked to fall to a price you set, buys a small amount, then guards each position with a stop-loss and a take-profit.
solToStart: about 0.3 SOL, the budget you give it
howItWorks: You list the coins it may buy in watchlist.json, and put the same mints in the policy's coins.allow. It never picks coins from chat, comments or trending lists.
For each coin it runs a rug check first, and skips any that fails.
It places a limit buy: a set amount of SOL, filled only once the on-chain price falls a set share below today's (20% to start), and closed after 7 days if it never does.
When a buy fills, it places a stop-loss and a take-profit on what it bought. When one of them fills, it cancels the other.
After a cooldown it re-arms that coin, at most a few rounds per coin, and never past the policy's daily cap.
earns: Nothing by itself. It buys after a fall and sells after a rise or a further fall, and any round can lose. Each round pays the coin's trading fee both ways (1% on a New school curve) and Highwire's 0.3% both ways, so a take-profit has to clear them. The calculator shows what a win and a loss come to.
costs: No launch, so no launch fee.
Each buy and sell: the coin's trading fee (1% on a New school curve, 0.25% on Old school, about 0.3% after graduation), Solana network fees, and Highwire's 0.3%.
Limit buys, stop-losses and take-profits cost nothing until they fill.
needs: A machine that stays on to run the order runner
A few coins you chose yourself, by mint address
risks: A coin that falls 20% can keep falling. The stop-loss limits the loss, but sells at the price when it triggers, within the slippage cap.
Thin coins can move straight past a trigger; with a tight slippage cap the order waits while the price runs away.
Orders fill only while the order runner is running.
Fees on both sides mean small moves lose money.

milestones.title: M1 · The watchlist and dry-run buys
milestones.summary: watchlist.json, a rug check for each coin, and one limit buy per coin placed against a dry-run policy.

milestones.title: M2 · Guarding the positions
milestones.summary: After each fill, a stop-loss and a take-profit; when one fills, the other is cancelled.

milestones.title: M3 · Going live (you)
milestones.summary: Fund the wallet with the budget, check coins.allow, and set live.

milestones.title: M4 · Rounds and a daily summary
milestones.summary: Cooldowns, a cap on rounds per coin, and a plain summary of profit and loss each day.

prompt: Read PRD.md and AGENTS.md, then build milestone 1. Keep the policy a dry run: never set "live" yourself.

day.text: You deploy the template, run setup, and write watchlist.json with two or three coins you chose. You add the same mints to the policy's coins.allow.
The agent rug-checks each coin and places one limit buy for each: 0.05 SOL, if the price falls 20%. As a dry run, a trigger is checked and simulated, and nothing is sent.
The order runner sees the price at the trigger on-chain and buys. The agent then places a stop-loss 15% below the fill and a take-profit 40% above it.
One of the two fills and sells the position. The agent cancels the other, waits a day, and re-arms the coin if it has rounds left.
It prints a summary: rounds done, profit and loss per coin from get_wallet_pnl, and what's still waiting.
Create the STOP file and nothing more is signed. Every order, fill and refusal is in the audit log.

policyNotes.actions: Trades only: no launches, claims or transfers.
policyNotes.max_sol_per_tx: The most one buy can spend. Keep it at or above the watchlist's buy size.
policyNotes.max_sol_per_day: The most a day of buys can ever spend, whatever triggers.
policyNotes.max_slippage_bps: 5%: dips are when coins move fastest.
policyNotes.coins: Empty to start, so nothing can be bought. You add the watchlist's mints yourself.
policyNotes.orders: Limit buys, stop-losses and take-profits, at most nine open: three for each of three coins.

faq.q: Does it pick coins for me?
faq.a: No. You choose the coins, and the policy's coins.allow is the only list it can buy from. It never takes a coin from chat, comments, names or trending lists.

faq.q: Is this a way to make money?
faq.a: It's a way to automate a rule you already want to follow. Buying dips loses money when coins keep falling, and fees take a share of every round. Run it as a dry run first, and with a budget you can lose.

faq.q: What happens if the order runner is off when the price dips?
faq.a: Nothing fills while it's off. When it starts again it checks prices fresh and fills only orders whose trigger is met then.

faq.q: Can it spend more than the budget?
faq.a: No. Each buy is checked against max_sol_per_tx and max_sol_per_day, from the audit log, and refused past them, even when an order triggers.

faq.q: Why does a dry run need the coins in the policy?
faq.a: A dry run checks the policy exactly as a live run does, so it tells you the truth about what would happen. Until a mint is in coins.allow, Highwire refuses it.
Create the STOP file (~/.highwire/dip-buyer/STOP), or set the policy back to a dry run. Cancel orders with npm run highwire -- orders cancel <id>.
